To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have crystallized the native and saponified proteins and have collected diffraction data to 2.1 and 2.2 Angstroms, respectively, and have collected MAD data for the native selenomethione-substituted protein.

we crystallized and solved the structure of a novel transcriptional regulator, the TBP-interacting factor from the archaeon Thermococcales, and that this protein has a novel fold that is different from that of the known TBP-interacting factors from eubacteria and eukaryotes.
the 26 kDa Tk-TIP26 protein from the hyperthrmophilic archaeon T. kodakaraensis was crystallized and the structure was solved using MAD phasing.

the crystallization and preliminary Xray analysis of the TIP26 protein from Thermococcus kodaka...
the structure determination of Tk-TIP26.
the structural and functional studies of Tk-TIP26, which will contribute to a better understanding of transcription regulation mechanisms in the Thermococcales.

the crystallization of TBP-interaction proteins from hyperthermophillic archaea is possible, which will be helpful for the study of the mechanism of TBP-interactions in hyperthermophilc archaea.
